title: MSCS overview: total credits and track options
text: The NYIT catalog’s Computer Science, M.S. program page describes the program as 30 total credits and introduces thesis/non-thesis paths and program goals. Use for top-level MSCS credit questions and orientation to options.

title: MSCS overview: core vs remaining credits (conceptual)
text: The MSCS overview explains that a portion of the credits are required CS coursework and the remaining credits are used for electives/specialization or thesis path planning. Use this chunk when users ask how credits are distributed (high level).

title: MSCS curriculum: total required credits
text: The MSCS curriculum requirements page lists Total Required Credits and outlines course-selection patterns for thesis vs non-thesis options.

title: MSCS curriculum: thesis sequence
text: The curriculum page includes thesis course sequence entries and describes how thesis credits fit into the 30-credit plan. Use for questions about thesis pathway structure.

title: MSCS curriculum: non-thesis elective selection
text: The curriculum page describes how non-thesis students complete required courses plus elective credits, with elective options depending on catalog year and availability. Use for general non-thesis planning guidance.

title: Graduation steps: requirements + application
text: NYIT’s Graduation & Diplomas page outlines fulfilling catalog requirements, meeting minimum GPA requirements, applying for graduation via Student Service HUB, and advisor recommendation via degree-audit evaluation submitted to the Registrar.

title: Graduation steps: advisor recommendation & degree audit
text: The graduation guidance emphasizes advisor recommendation and a signed degree audit evaluation as part of the approval workflow. Use for questions about who approves and what documents are needed.

title: Manage schedule: add/drop overview
text: NYIT’s Manage Your Schedule page explains add/drop as the period when students can adjust schedules and points students to the Academic Calendar for exact dates for their term/session.

title: Manage schedule: withdrawal and W grade
text: After add/drop ends, NYIT describes schedule changes as withdrawals, which result in a W grade. The page points to Academic Calendar deadlines and related procedures.

title: Academic Calendar: authoritative dates
text: NYIT’s Academic Calendar lists date-specific deadlines (add/drop, withdrawal, graduation application, etc.). Use this for any question that depends on the calendar date.

title: Student Service HUB: overview
text: NYIT describes the Student Service HUB as a one-stop home for student business tasks like registration, billing, financial aid, and grades.

title: Advising: how to view To Dos and Holds
text: NYIT’s advising guidance explains how students can view To Dos and Holds via my.nyit.edu and Student Service HUB (My Tasks), and suggests clicking each item for resolution steps.

title: Academic policies: graduate GPA / academic notice
text: NYIT’s Academic Policies include graduate academic notice information and graduation GPA requirements for graduate students. Use for GPA/standing questions.

title: Academic policies: repeats, standing, grading (pointer)
text: NYIT’s Academic Policies page is the central reference for academic standing, grade policies, and related rules. Use as a retrieval anchor when users ask about repeats/incompletes/standing.

title: Policies & Rules: catalog notice
text: NYIT’s Policies & Rules section includes a notice about catalog policies being binding and about the institution’s right to change policies and requirements. Use for catalog-year and policy applicability questions.

title: Tuition adjustment: add/drop
text: NYIT’s add/drop tuition adjustment policy describes how tuition adjustments depend on timing and session format. Use when users ask about refunds during add/drop.

title: Tuition adjustment: withdrawal/dismissal
text: NYIT’s withdrawal/dismissal tuition adjustment policy describes timing-based tuition adjustments for withdrawals/dismissals. Use when users ask about refund outcomes after withdrawal.

title: Registrar form: Withdrawal From Course
text: NYIT’s Withdrawal From Course form supports the withdrawal process and flags that withdrawal can have impacts beyond academics (e.g., financial aid or international student considerations).

title: Registrar form: Withdraw From All Courses
text: NYIT’s Withdraw From All Courses form provides instructions for withdrawing from all courses for a term and is used for full-term withdrawal requests.

title: Registrar form: Permission to Take Courses at Another College
text: NYIT’s permission form describes prerequisites for taking courses elsewhere for transfer credit (course description/credits, applicability, signatures). Use for current-student transfer planning.

title: Transfer credits: incoming student evaluation
text: NYIT’s transfer credits page describes post-admission transcript review and a personalized course-by-course evaluation applicable to the student’s major.

title: Transfer credit tool: current student note
text: NYIT’s transfer credit evaluator page points current students to complete the Permission to Take Courses at Another College process before enrolling elsewhere for transfer credit.

title: Graduate credit transfer policy
text: NYIT’s Graduate Credit Transfer Policy explains that graduate transfer credit decisions are program-dependent and will be evaluated with the student’s program needs in mind.

title: Graduate SAP policy: qualitative + quantitative standards
text: NYIT’s Graduate Satisfactory Academic Progress policy describes qualitative (GPA) and quantitative (pace/completion) standards used to evaluate aid eligibility.

title: Undergraduate SAP policy: GPA + pace standards
text: NYIT’s Undergraduate SAP policy describes minimum cumulative GPA and completion-rate (pace) standards for aid eligibility.

title: Graduate admissions: selected grad credits before BA/BS completion
text: NYIT’s graduate admissions information describes an option for eligible students to enroll in selected graduate credits before completing an undergraduate degree, with details coordinated via program leadership.

title: Manage schedule: where to check dates
text: The Manage Your Schedule page repeatedly points students to the Academic Calendar for exact dates and deadlines; use it as a process overview + calendar pointer.

title: HUB: where To Dos/Holds live
text: The Student Service HUB centralizes student tasks; holds and To Dos are typically handled within HUB workflows and My Tasks.

title: Advising: general support entry point
text: NYIT advising resources serve as the entry point for academic planning questions; use it to route students to advising help when policy is program-specific.

title: Policies & Rules: where to find official policy pages
text: NYIT’s Policies & Rules section links to official policy pages (academic policies, grading, and other rules). Use as a retrieval hub for policy questions.

title: About NYIT: University Overview
text: NYIT (New York Institute of Technology) is a private, independent, nonprofit, non-sectarian, coeducational research university founded in 1955. NYIT has over 8,000 students in programs leading to bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees in more than 90 subjects. The university has campuses on Long Island and in Manhattan, as well as international locations.

title: MSCS Program: Master of Science in Computer Science
text: The Master of Science in Computer Science program at NYIT is a 30-credit graduate degree program offered by the Department of Computer Science in the College of Engineering and Computing Sciences. The program prepares students for careers in software development, artificial intelligence, data science, cybersecurity, and other computing fields. Students can choose between thesis and non-thesis options.

title: MSCS Curriculum: Required and Elective Courses
text: The MSCS curriculum consists of core required courses in algorithms, software engineering, and computing theory, plus elective courses that allow students to specialize in areas such as Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Cloud Computing, and Software Development. Students complete 30 credits total, distributed between required courses and electives based on their chosen track.

title: College of Engineering and Computing Sciences Locations
text: The College of Engineering and Computing Sciences offers programs at NYIT's Old Westbury (Long Island) campus and Manhattan campus. Graduate students in Computer Science can take classes at either location. The department provides state-of-the-art laboratories, research facilities, and collaborative spaces for graduate students.

title: MSCS Admissions: Requirements and Prerequisites
text: Admission to the MSCS program requires a bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field, undergraduate transcripts showing strong academic performance, letters of recommendation, and a statement of purpose. Students without a CS background may need to complete prerequisite courses. International students must also meet English proficiency requirements.

title: MSCS Career Outcomes and Opportunities
text: The Master of Science in Computer Science prepares graduates for advanced careers in software development, artificial intelligence, machine learning, data science, cybersecurity, cloud computing, and systems architecture. Graduates work at major technology companies, financial institutions, healthcare organizations, government agencies, and startups. The program provides both theoretical foundations and practical skills needed for leadership roles in technology.

title: Student Service HUB: Central Portal for All Student Business
text: The Student Service HUB at my.nyit.edu is your one-stop portal for all university business. Through the HUB, students can register for classes, view grades, check financial aid, pay bills, update personal information, view holds and to-do items, access their degree audit, and communicate with advisors. The HUB consolidates previously separate systems into a single, convenient interface for managing your academic life at NYIT.

title: Common Registration Holds and How to Resolve Them
text: Registration holds prevent students from enrolling in classes until specific requirements are met. The most common holds include: Financial Hold (unpaid balance - contact Bursar at 516.686.7510), Advising Hold (must meet with advisor - schedule appointment through HUB), Admissions Hold (missing documents - contact admissions@nyit.edu), Immunization Hold (missing health records - contact Student Health Services), and Prerequisite Hold (course requirements not met - verify with Registrar). All holds are visible in the My Tasks section of Student Service HUB with resolution instructions.

title: Academic Calendar: Key Dates and Deadlines
text: The Academic Calendar is the authoritative source for all important dates at NYIT, including semester start and end dates, add/drop deadlines, withdrawal deadlines, holidays, final exam periods, and graduation application deadlines. Dates vary by term type (fall/spring semester vs. summer sessions and cycle courses). Students should consult the calendar specific to their enrollment term. Missing deadlines can result in financial penalties, inability to drop courses, or delayed graduation.

title: Academic Advising Process and Best Practices
text: Academic advising at NYIT follows a shared responsibility model. Faculty advisors provide discipline-specific guidance and approve course selections. Professional advisors assist with degree requirements, policy interpretation, and graduation planning. Students should meet with their advisor at least once per semester before registration. To prepare for advising appointments, students should review their degree audit, plan tentative course schedules, bring questions about degree requirements, and be prepared to discuss academic and career goals. Advisors release registration holds after approving course selections.

title: Step-by-Step Registration Process
text: Registration at NYIT follows these steps: 1) Meet with your academic advisor to select courses and release your advising hold. 2) Check your enrollment appointment time in Student Service HUB. 3) Use Schedule Planner to build your ideal schedule by selecting preferred times and days. 4) Use the Validate Schedule feature to check for conflicts, holds, and prerequisite issues. 5) Send your validated schedule to the shopping cart. 6) Review your shopping cart and complete enrollment. 7) Verify your schedule and make any needed changes during the add/drop period. Registration is not complete until all steps are finished and you receive confirmation.

title: Schedule Planner Tool: Features and Benefits
text: Schedule Planner is an interactive tool in Student Service HUB that helps students build optimal class schedules. Features include: selecting preferred days and times, planning breaks between classes, viewing multiple schedule options simultaneously, checking seat availability in real-time, validating prerequisites and corequisites automatically, and avoiding time conflicts. The tool generates several possible schedules based on your preferences, allowing you to compare options before enrolling. Once satisfied, send your preferred schedule directly to your shopping cart for enrollment.

title: Financial Aid and Satisfactory Academic Progress
text: To maintain financial aid eligibility, students must meet Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) standards. For graduate students, this includes maintaining a minimum cumulative GPA (typically 3.0) and completing at least 67% of attempted credits (pace requirement). Students who fail to meet SAP standards receive a warning and may lose aid eligibility if standards are not met in subsequent terms. Appeals are possible for extenuating circumstances. Withdrawals, incompletes, and repeated courses all affect SAP calculations. Students should consult with Financial Aid before making enrollment changes that might impact aid eligibility.

title: Course Withdrawal Policies and Procedures
text: Students may withdraw from courses after the add/drop period by submitting a Withdrawal from Course form to their instructor. Withdrawals result in a W grade on the transcript, which does not affect GPA but counts toward attempted credits. Withdrawal deadlines are published in the Academic Calendar and vary by session type. Late withdrawals may not be approved except for documented emergencies. Students should consider the financial, academic, and immigration implications before withdrawing. Withdrawing may affect financial aid, enrollment status, degree progress, and graduation timeline. Consult advisors and relevant offices before withdrawing from courses.

title: Tutoring and Academic Support Resources
text: NYIT provides comprehensive tutoring and academic support through multiple channels. The Academic Success Center offers free peer tutoring in many subjects, both in-person and online. Faculty office hours provide one-on-one help from instructors. Supplemental Instruction (SI) sessions are available for historically difficult courses, led by students who previously excelled in those courses. Writing support is available through the Writing Center for all stages of the writing process. Students can schedule appointments through the Academic Success portal or attend drop-in tutoring hours. Early and regular use of tutoring services correlates strongly with academic success.

title: Requirements for Degree Completion and Graduation
text: To graduate from NYIT, students must: 1) Complete all required credits for their program with required minimum GPA (typically 3.0 for graduate programs, 2.0 for undergraduate). 2) Fulfill all major, core, and elective requirements as specified in the catalog. 3) Meet residency requirements (minimum credits taken at NYIT). 4) Resolve all financial obligations and holds. 5) Submit an application for graduation through Student Service HUB by the published deadline for their intended graduation term. 6) Receive recommendation from their academic department based on a degree audit evaluation. The Registrar's office conducts a final review before degrees are conferred.

title: Course Repeat Policy and Grade Replacement
text: Students may repeat courses to improve their grades, subject to program-specific policies. When a course is repeated, typically the higher grade is used in GPA calculations, though both attempts remain on the transcript. Some programs limit the number of courses that can be repeated or the number of repeat attempts allowed. Repeated courses count toward attempted credits for financial aid and SAP calculations. Students should verify their specific program's repeat policy with their advisor before retaking courses. Prerequisites and graduation requirements may specify minimum grades that cannot be met by repeating courses in some cases.

title: International Student Enrollment and Status Requirements
text: International students on F-1 visas must maintain full-time enrollment status each semester (typically 9 credits for graduate students, 12 for undergraduate). Dropping below full-time status without authorization can jeopardize visa status. International students should consult the Office of International Education before making any enrollment changes, including withdrawing from courses, adding/dropping courses, or taking reduced course loads. Reduced course loads may be approved for specific circumstances such as final semester, academic difficulties, or medical reasons, but require proper documentation and approval before implementation.

title: Academic Honors and Recognition
text: NYIT recognizes academic excellence through several honors programs. Dean's List honors students who achieve high GPAs during a semester while enrolled full-time. Graduation honors (summa cum laude, magna cum laude, cum laude) are awarded based on cumulative GPA at graduation. Honor societies like Phi Kappa Phi recognize overall academic achievement across disciplines. Many academic departments have discipline-specific honor societies. Academic honors appear on transcripts and are recognized at commencement. Criteria for honors vary by program and level; students should consult their academic advisor for specific requirements.

title: Changing Academic Programs or Campus Location
text: Students wishing to change their major must complete the Application to Change Undergraduate Major form (undergraduates) or contact their graduate program director (graduate students). The process requires approval from both current and new programs. Students should meet with advisors from both programs to understand implications for degree progress, as requirements may differ significantly between programs. To change campus locations, students complete the Application to Change Campus form. Campus changes may affect course availability, program options, and student services access. Both major and campus changes can impact financial aid, scholarships, and graduation timeline.
